scope: Final staged 0.5.3 catalog, native-matching pack inventory and all declared asset hashes; six aligner/caller integration tests containing four composed successful DAGs and all 23 declared scientific installation cases, plus 62 core regressions. Scientific commands executed on Linux only: actual shipped portable SAMtools, BCFtools, paircheck and LoFreq through pinned APE loader; separately pinned Linux Bowtie2/HISAT2/Java/Perl/SeqKit/VSEARCH/MUSCLE references. VarDict Java classpath separators alone translated to Linux syntax. No Windows execution is claimed.

executedGraphs.name: Compare aligners with separately attributed SNP reports
executedGraphs.methods:
Executed methods (only successfully completed operations are described):

Step S1 (Map the known read pairs) was performed using align-s 2.5.5; build-s 2.5.5; paircheck 1.0.1 (pack bowtie2 0.5.3). A private copy of the reference was indexed with Bowtie 2 using 32-bit small index files. Mate identifiers, counts and FASTQ structure were validated with paircheck. Reads were aligned end to end with Bowtie 2, interpreting quality scores as Phred+33 and using the selected sensitivity preset and deterministic seed. The specified fragment bounds and orientation governed concordant pairing; Bowtie 2 discordant-pair and single-mate fallback were enabled. At most one primary alignment was reported per read, with unmapped reads retained. SAM records include the selected sample, read group, library and sequencing-platform tags. Output order follows input order and is not coordinate sorted. Settings: Sample name=validation; Read-group ID=lane1; Library ID=library1; Sequencing platform=ILLUMINA; End-to-end search effort=sensitive; Threads=1; Random seed=42; Expected mate orientation=fr; Minimum fragment length=0; Maximum fragment length=500. Inputs: Read 1: I1 · Sixty pairs; 20 percent SNP alleles | Reference genome: I2 · Known synthetic reference.

Step S4 (HISAT2 DNA branch) was performed using hisat2-align-l 2.2.3-workbench1; hisat2-build-l 2.2.3-workbench1; paircheck 1.0.1 (pack hisat2 0.5.3). Reads were aligned to a privately indexed genomic reference using HISAT2 2.2.3-workbench1 and its 64-bit linear index. Spliced alignment was disabled (--no-spliced-alignment), producing unsorted DNA SAM. Phred+33 input, read-group metadata, CPU count and alignment seed were explicit; duplicates were retained. Settings: Sample ID=validation; Read-group ID=lane1; Library ID=lib1; Platform unit / lane=unit1; Sequencing platform=ILLUMINA; HISAT2 CPU threads=1; Alignment seed=0; Minimum DNA fragment length=0; Maximum DNA fragment length=500. Inputs: Paired FASTQ reads: I1 · Sixty pairs; 20 percent SNP alleles | Reference genome: I2 · Known synthetic reference.

Step S2 (Prepare DNA alignments) was performed using samtools 1.24 (pack bam 0.4.0). Name-sort, fix mates, coordinate-sort, mark duplicates, index and summarize. Duplicates are retained. Inputs: Paired alignments: S1 · Map the known read pairs → Read alignments (unsorted SAM).

Step S5 (Prepare paired alignments) was performed using samtools 1.24 (pack bam 0.4.0). Name-sort, fix mates, coordinate-sort, mark duplicates, index and summarize. Duplicates are retained. Inputs: Paired alignments: S4 · HISAT2 DNA branch → Unsorted DNA alignments.

Step S3 (Call low-frequency SNPs) was performed using lofreq 2.1.5-workbench-port2; samtools 1.24 (pack lofreq 0.5.3). LoFreq called SNVs only with the configured mapping/base-quality, coverage, depth and significance thresholds, extended BAQ, dynamic Bonferroni correction and default post-call filters (minimum coverage 10 and strand-bias FDR). Only PASS sites were retained. The VCF contains observed read allele frequencies and site error-model significance, not sample genotypes or a ploidy model; low-frequency calls require assay-specific validation. Settings: Minimum mapping quality=20; Minimum reference and alternate base quality=20; Minimum tested coverage=10; Maximum pileup depth=1000000; Significance level=0.01. Inputs: Coordinate-sorted DNA alignments: S2 · Prepare DNA alignments → Sorted, duplicate-marked BAM | Reference genome: I2 · Known synthetic reference.

Step S6 (LoFreq: low-frequency SNVs) was performed using lofreq 2.1.5-workbench-port2; samtools 1.24 (pack lofreq 0.5.3). LoFreq called SNVs only with the configured mapping/base-quality, coverage, depth and significance thresholds, extended BAQ, dynamic Bonferroni correction and default post-call filters (minimum coverage 10 and strand-bias FDR). Only PASS sites were retained. The VCF contains observed read allele frequencies and site error-model significance, not sample genotypes or a ploidy model; low-frequency calls require assay-specific validation. Settings: Minimum mapping quality=20; Minimum reference and alternate base quality=20; Minimum tested coverage=10; Maximum pileup depth=1000000; Significance level=0.01. Inputs: Coordinate-sorted DNA alignments: S5 · Prepare paired alignments → Sorted, duplicate-marked BAM | Reference genome: I2 · Known synthetic reference.

Step S7 (Bowtie2-based calls) was performed using bcftools 1.24 (pack variants 0.4.0). Summarize an existing VCF or BCF. Inputs: Variants: S3 · Call low-frequency SNPs → PASS site-only variants (no genotypes).

Step S8 (HISAT2-based calls) was performed using bcftools 1.24 (pack variants 0.4.0). Summarize an existing VCF or BCF. Inputs: Variants: S6 · LoFreq: low-frequency SNVs → PASS site-only variants (no genotypes).

Step S9 (Combine statistics reports) was performed using Combine statistics reports (pack builtin 0.5.0). Collect selected statistics into a local HTML report with a separate, attributed section for each input. Counts are not pooled and variant files are not merged. Settings: Report title=Separate aligner results. Inputs: Statistics to include: S7 · Bowtie2-based calls → Variant statistics; S8 · HISAT2-based calls → Variant statistics.

Tool references:
Langmead B, Salzberg SL. Fast gapped-read alignment with Bowtie 2. Nature Methods 9, 357–359 (2012). https://doi.org/10.1038/nmeth.1923
Kim D, Paggi JM, Park C, Bennett C and Salzberg SL (2019). Graph-based genome alignment and genotyping with HISAT2 and HISAT-genotype. Nature Biotechnology 37:907-915. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41587-019-0201-4
Wilm et al. (2012). LoFreq: a sequence-quality aware, ultra-sensitive variant caller for uncovering cell-population heterogeneity from high-throughput sequencing datasets. Nucleic Acids Research 40:11189–11201. https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/gks918
Albers et al. (2011). Dindel: accurate indel calls from short-read data. Genome Research 21:961–973. https://doi.org/10.1101/gr.112326.110

executedGraphs.methods:
Executed methods (only successfully completed operations are described):

Step S1 (Map the known read pairs) was performed using align-s 2.5.5; build-s 2.5.5; paircheck 1.0.1 (pack bowtie2 0.5.3). Inputs: Coordinate-sorted DNA alignments: S2 · Prepare DNA alignments → Sorted, duplicate-marked BAM | Reference genome: I2 · Known synthetic reference.

Step S4 (VarDict targeted calls) was performed using bcftools 1.24; java 8u504-b01; perl 5.42.3.1; samtools 1.24 (pack vardict 0.5.3). Single-sample targeted variants were called with VarDictJava 1.8.3 using local realignment and the upstream EXPERIMENTAL --fisher implementation of strand-bias Fisher tests. Structural-variant calling was disabled. Coordinate-sorted DNA BAM and nonoverlapping BED4 targets were used with the recorded quality, depth and allele-fraction settings. The unmodified upstream var2vcf_valid.pl script bundled with release 1.8.3 (script version 1.8.2) converted every candidate allele (-A) to VCF, retaining FILTER labels; its allele-fraction-based diploid genotype convention was retained (homozygous ALT above 80% AF). This does not determine somatic status or support arbitrary ploidy. BCFtools checked REF alleles, left-aligned/split calls, compressed/indexed all calls and separately exported PASS calls. The Java Fisher path was compared with R on finite deterministic fixtures but remains experimental upstream. Settings: Sample name (BAM SM)=validation; Minimum candidate allele fraction=0.02; VCF minimum total depth=8; Minimum alternate-supporting reads=3; Good-base Phred quality=25; Minimum read mapping quality=20; VCF minimum mean read position=8; Threads=1; Maximum Java heap (MiB)=1024. Inputs: Prepared coordinate-sorted single-sample BAM: S2 · Prepare DNA alignments → Sorted, duplicate-marked BAM | Matching reference genome: I2 · Known synthetic reference | Target intervals (BED4): I3 · Known target interval.

Step S5 (LoFreq call statistics) was performed using bcftools 1.24 (pack variants 0.4.0). Summarize an existing VCF or BCF. Inputs: Variants: S3 · Call low-frequency SNPs → PASS site-only variants (no genotypes).

Step S6 (Combine statistics reports) was performed using Combine statistics reports (pack builtin 0.5.0). Collect selected statistics into a local HTML report with a separate, attributed section for each input. Counts are not pooled and variant files are not merged. Settings: Report title=Independent caller results. Inputs: Statistics to include: S5 · LoFreq call statistics → Variant statistics; S4 · VarDict targeted calls → All-call statistics.

limitations: Linux reference execution does not validate Windows launch/runtime behavior.
Small deterministic synthetic fixtures exercise the declared transformations and interfaces; they do not establish accuracy on all organisms, samples or clinical settings.
Single-sample alignment validation checks read-group header metadata, not RG tags on every record.
Reference dictionaries without M5 hashes do not prove reference base identity.
VarDict built-in Fisher mode remains explicitly experimental in its recorded methods.
